briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 13, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Weather Events and Global Threats
sections.content: Today's main news is a warning about the intensifying extreme weather events worldwide. Climate scientists emphasize that climate change is increasing the likelihood of extreme weather [61, 73, 87], and domestically, heatwaves are changing daily life, with a record-breaking temperature of 42.5℃ observed in Yangsan, Gyeongnam, in the summer of 2026 [43]. In southern Brazil, the direct impacts of climate change continue, with 183 deaths and over 600,000 people displaced by floods in May 2024 [91]. Climate change has also led to entirely new types of heatwaves, such as 'snow-eating heatwaves' [56]. These extreme climates are further worsening already poor working conditions [53, 67], and legal actions are emerging, with Colorado ranchers supporting lawsuits holding fossil fuel companies accountable for land damage caused by climate change [68].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Policies and Implementation Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, policy efforts to achieve carbon neutrality goals are actively underway. The National Assembly's Special Committee on Climate passed the 'Carbon Neutrality Act' and the 'Climate Crisis Adaptation Act' by bipartisan agreement, with the amendment to the Carbon Neutrality Act specifically setting carbon reduction targets of 69-80% by 2040 [10, 12, 15]. Local government achievements are prominent, with Seocheon-gun and Changwon-si exceeding their greenhouse gas reduction targets and being selected as best practices [13, 17]. Sacheon-si, Gyeongju Carbon Neutrality Center, Gwangmyeong-si Residents' Autonomy Association, among others, are conducting education and campaigns for future generations [11, 21, 23, 41], and the government is promoting carbon neutrality projects to resolve power shortages through 'Power Shuttle' [9, 19]. However, during the implementation of these policies, criticisms such as 'public discourse being sidelined' [25] and critical commentaries on the passing of the Carbon Neutrality Act amendment [18] have been raised, highlighting the need for social discussion.

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Current Challenges
sections.content: The expansion of renewable energy is a key task in responding to the climate crisis, and its importance is being further highlighted both domestically and internationally. In Europe, the rapid increase in renewable energy facilities is leading to a decrease in natural gas demand [27]. Domestically, Paju-si directly supplies public renewable energy to support local companies' RE100 initiatives [28, 42], and Yongin Special City has achieved the best performance for four consecutive years in renewable energy support and post-management [31, 34]. Companies such as Samsung C&T and Osstem Implant are also expanding their participation through investments and increased production related to renewable energy [29, 39]. However, while improvements to setback distance regulations for renewable energy facilities are being discussed [26, 32], some criticisms are being raised that renewable energy is 'anti-environmental, burdening living environments' and imposes unilateral sacrifices without reflecting residents' opinions [30, 33, 35]. Furthermore, along with questions about whether renewable energy can meet the increasing power demand in the AI era [38], stably securing abundant renewable energy has emerged as an important challenge [40].

sections.title: 🌍 Scientific Understanding of Climate Change and International Response
sections.content: Efforts to enhance the scientific understanding of climate change and seek international cooperation are also ongoing. Paleoclimate experts emphasize the importance of studying the past to understand the future of climate change, citing Wyoming fossil research that showed ancient forests took 100,000 years to recover after past global warming periods [46, 54]. Research results have also been published indicating that the speed of climate change affects the stability of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) [55]. There is also interesting research suggesting that climate change determined apex predators approximately 35 million years ago [52]. Meanwhile, claims regarding the impact of climate change on harmful fungi or crop yields are being verified through fact-checking [57, 62]. Internationally, the U.S. Supreme Court has decided to hear state climate change lawsuits [72], and discussions on climate justice are also active, with questions being raised about whether Western countries should pay climate change reparations to Pakistan [77].

sections.title: 🌱 Climate Adaptation Economy and Innovative Responses
sections.content: Even amidst the crisis awareness of climate change, new economic opportunities and innovative adaptation strategies are being explored. Analysis suggests that extreme weather events like heatwaves and wildfires have, in fact, created a $20 trillion 'climate adaptation economy' market [2, 8]. In line with these changes, adaptation efforts are also appearing in the agricultural sector, such as the cultivation of golden apples called 'Golden Ball' in Gunwi, Korea, due to climate change [4]. Furthermore, innovative approaches utilizing advanced technology are active, such as the cultivation of high-protein spirulina adapted to climate change using Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology [6]. Creative attempts for climate adaptation are also continuing in urban environments, with Busan City launching the 'Beautiful Landscape Award' competition to select works responding to climate change [3]. Activities where artists reflect on climate change through play with sunlight are also noteworthy [74].

briefing.closing: As we have seen in today's briefing, climate change is a global threat that simultaneously demands humanity's continuous efforts and innovation to overcome it. Continued attention and action are crucial. This concludes today's climate briefing.
